content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-t06-ya6lbcbr/report.rdl

Turn the table into a matrix: sites down the side, equipment types across the top, operating hours in the cells, and 'Site' in the top-left corner.

The table is now a matrix on `FleetTable`:

- **Top-left corner:** "Site"
- **Rows:** one per site (`=Fields!Site.Value`)
- **Columns:** one per equipment type (`=Fields!EquipmentType.Value`)
- **Cells:** `=Sum(Fields!OperatingHours.Value)`

The report validates against the schema. The lint warnings (unused LegacySQL and ScratchPowerQuery data sources, DateFrom/DateTo typed as String, and a Utilization field the DAX doesn't return) were already there and I left them alone.

The old table also showed AssetName, IdleHours and Utilization. A matrix can't show per-asset rows, and you asked for only sites, equipment types and operating hours, so those three columns are gone from the layout. The dataset still returns them, so they can be added back if you need them.

The matrix's column width is 1.5in for the site column and 1in per equipment type, but the tablix width is still 6in. Equipment types are generated at render time, so the matrix will grow past 6in if there are more than about five types. I didn't change the tablix width, so you may want to adjust it or the page layout.
